v11.73 - x-119: önizlemenin reddettiği taslak artık başlatılamıyor

`previewMission` resolved every participant through the delegation ladder and
collected everything that would refuse the draft — an engine this machine cannot
run, an engine+effort pair the CLI has no flag for — and `createMission` ran
none of it. The two shared `resolveMissionInput` and nothing else, so the refusal
set was a property of LOOKING rather than of the mission: the same payload the
form was drawing "This draft would be refused" for created a spec, a run and its
tasks through the Start button and through `missions.start`, and the refusal
arrived one delegation at a time, after the planner had already spent its turns
deciding who does what.

`planMissionLaunch` is now the one answer both doors eat: the resolved spec and
the preview of it, refusals included. `previewMission` returns its preview and
writes nothing; `createMission` refuses a non-empty `problems` with the same
sentence the preview reports, all faults at once, before `startMission` touches
a store. `missions.start` says so in its describe, so a bridge caller cannot
read the preview as advisory.

Consequence worth knowing on an adaptive whole-fleet pool: one agent resolving
onto an engine this machine cannot run now refuses the whole mission up front
instead of failing that delegation mid-run. That is this codebase's own rule
("a mission that plans three rounds and then fails every delegation has spent
planner turns to discover something one disk read knew") applied to the members
as it already was to the mission-wide engine; the way out is the row's own
engine box or a narrower pool.

Measured in test/test_bridge.js: one resolution and one refusal set, the create
gate placed BEFORE startMission, and the describe that tells a caller the two
doors refuse alike.
